headline: Keep the longest window with at most two fruit types
statement: Pick one fruit from each consecutive tree while moving right from any chosen start. Two baskets each hold one fruit type with unlimited capacity. Return the greatest number picked before a third type would be required.
intuition: The basket rule means the chosen segment contains at most two distinct values. Grow a window rightward; if a third type appears, remove leftmost fruits until one type disappears. The remaining window is the longest legal one ending here.
approach: While more than two types remain, decrement the leftmost type and move left.
Remove a type from the map when its count reaches zero.
Update the largest legal window length.
correctness: After shrinking, the window contains at most two types. Its left boundary is the earliest feasible start for that right endpoint: earlier starts still contain the third type that forced shrinking. Any optimal segment has some right endpoint, so comparing the longest feasible window at every endpoint finds the global optimum.
bruteForce: Try each starting tree and extend until the third type, taking O(n²) in the worst case.

complexity.explanation: Each pointer moves at most n steps; the map holds at most three types during adjustment.

pitfalls: The chosen trees must be consecutive.
Delete zero-count keys so distinct-type count is accurate.
Baskets constrain types, not the number of individual fruits.
